slides.title: Is Telehealth Better Used to Treat Patients or Help Other Physicians Treat Patients? An Agent-Based Modeling Study of Healthcare Provision
slides.highlight: This study uses agent-based modeling to compare physician-physician and physician-patient telehealth, providing insights into societal-scale healthcare utilization relevant to MIMIC.

card.one_liner: Telehealth is more cost-effective for toxicologist-physician consultations than for direct toxicologist-patient care.
card.key_idea: An agent-based model simulating medical toxicology care to compare the health outcomes and costs of physician-facing versus patient-facing telehealth access points.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via 100 simulation runs (Mesa/Python) across various scenarios, measuring health improvement, hospital admissions, and cost per patient.
card.limitation: Relies on simulated data and an incomplete model assuming perfect in-hospital diagnostic accuracy and single medical problems per patient.

slides.title: Modelling Opinion Dynamics at Scale with Deep MARL
slides.highlight: This research utilizes multi-agent reinforcement learning to simulate opinion dynamics and conformity in large-scale social networks, contributing to the meso- and societal-scale simulation goals of MIMIC.

card.one_liner: Deep MARL models opinion dynamics to show how conformity in large networks promotes misinformation.
card.key_idea: A GPU-accelerated consensus and truth-finding game using general-sum other-play MARL and a learned attention layer to recover agent importance from graph topology.
card.evaluation: Validated on a Bluesky network subset; compared large social media networks against small hunter-gatherer networks to analyze collective accuracy.

slides.title: DyaPlex: Full-Duplex Speech-Motion Model for Dyadic Interaction
slides.highlight: DyaPlex enables simultaneous perception and generation of speech and physical motion in dyadic interactions, contributing to multimodal social perception of team states for HyECHO.

card.one_liner: DyaPlex is a streaming, full-duplex model for simultaneous perception and generation of dyadic speech and motion.
card.key_idea: A dual-tower Transformer coupling a frozen speech model with a trainable motion tower using dyadic token interleaving and time-aligned speech-motion RoPE for cross-modal synchronization.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the 4,000-hour Seamless Interaction dataset against A2P and DualTalk using FGD, P-FD, and BeatAlign; results show state-of-the-art performance.
card.limitation: The autoregressive motion tower is the primary computational bottleneck, requiring context window reduction to achieve real-time inference.

slides.title: Face versus Body Tracking for Human-Robot Interaction: An Egocentric Dataset
slides.tldr: EGO-CENTRIC DATASET FOR IMPROVING HRI TRACKING STABILITY
slides.highlight: This work introduces a custom egocentric dataset and evaluates face versus body tracking to reduce identity switches in social robots, supporting RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A new egocentric dataset and evaluation comparing face and body tracking for social robot interactions.
card.key_idea: Optimizes tracking by combining extended temporal memory and appearance ReID, finding that ReID stabilizes body tracking but destabilizes face tracking due to profile angle sensitivity.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 20 custom Furhat robot sequences using HOTA, IDF1, and IDSW metrics; optimized body pipeline reduced IDSW by 49% over baseline.
card.limitation: Limited to 20 indoor office sequences with a stationary robot and specific fisheye lens; real-time compute constraints were not assessed.

slides.title: Personality Anchoring for Social Simulation: Linking Personality, Social Behavior, and Interaction Success with LLM Agents
slides.tldr: PERSONALITY ANCHORING FOR LLM SOCIAL SIMULATION
slides.highlight: This research introduces a personality anchoring pipeline for multi-LLM social simulations, demonstrating how personality traits like Agreeableness influence goal achievement and cooperative strategies. This is relevant to MIMIC's use of LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: Personality anchoring using known characters reveals that dyadic Agreeableness strongly predicts shared goal achievement in LLM simulations.
card.key_idea: Agents are instantiated as well-known characters (personality anchoring) rather than via trait prompting, then interact across diverse goal-driven scenarios using structured behavior strategy selection.
card.evaluation: 1,010 conversations across 7 goal categories; evaluated via LLM-as-a-judge. Results show high consistency (ICC=0.89) and a monotonic relationship between Agreeableness and success.
card.limitation: Relies on LLM-as-a-judge scoring and pre-existing model knowledge of characters, which may introduce stereotypical biases and lack cultural diversity.

slides.title: Personalized and Robust Proactive Robot Assistance with Uncertainty-Guided LLM Reasoning
slides.tldr: PROACTIVE ROBOT ASSISTANCE VIA LLM REASONING
slides.highlight: The GLOBE framework improves proactive robot assistance in noisy household environments by combining Markov models with uncertainty-guided LLM reasoning. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied AI.

card.one_liner: GLOBE uses n-gram Markov models and selective LLM reasoning for robust, proactive household object prediction.
card.key_idea: A lightweight framework combining n-gram Markov models for temporal patterns with an LLM that is selectively triggered when prediction confidence falls below a threshold.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on HOMER+ and a new HOMER-Noise dataset against SLaTe-PRO and STOT using F1-scores; results show competitive accuracy and superior noise robustness.
card.limitation: Inference latency is significantly higher than baselines due to external LLM API calls.

slides.title: Vietnam's Vingroup Unveils Two Humanoid Robots
slides.highlight: The introduction of a guide bot and a factory bot by Vingroup provides examples of humanoid applications relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Titans-as-a-Layer: Test-Time Memory for Conversational Speech Emotion Recognition
slides.highlight: This work introduces a Memory-as-a-Layer adapter to capture dialogue history and emotional context, supporting HyECHO's goals in multimodal social perception and engagement modeling.

card.one_liner: A plug-and-play memory adapter improves conversational speech emotion recognition by maintaining dialogue-specific state at test-time.
card.key_idea: Memory-as-a-Layer (MAL) uses Titans-style neural memory to inject audio-token-aligned residual updates into frozen LALMs, trained sequentially after LoRA task adaptation.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on IEMOCAP, MELD, and MultiDialog using Qwen2-Audio, Audio Flamingo 3, and Ultravox-v0.4; showed consistent gains in WA, UA, and WF1.
card.limitation: Broader coverage across all backbone-dataset combinations and comparisons against other memory architectures are still required.

slides.title: Safe, Fluent and Acceptable Motion Generation and Execution for Human--Robot Interaction in Manufacturing Environments
slides.highlight: This research explores integrating social-aware motion control and human-centered considerations into robot behavior to improve social acceptability, supporting RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A motion control framework that generates socially-aware robot behaviors by modulating velocity and interaction distance.
card.key_idea: An MPC framework using separating-plane optimization and LSTM-based human motion prediction to implement four distinct behaviors based on maximum velocity and interaction distance parameters.
card.evaluation: Validated via a user study with 111 non-experts using NASA-TLX for workload and 10 bipolar adjective scales for social perception.

slides.title: Impedance MPC for Physical Human-Robot Interaction: Predictive Disturbance Rejection with Joint-Limit Safety
slides.tldr: PREDICTIVE IMPEDANCE CONTROL FOR SAFE PHRI
slides.highlight: This work introduces a two-layer Impedance MPC that achieves high trajectory accuracy and zero steady-state error during physical human-robot interaction. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A two-layer Impedance MPC achieving zero steady-state error and joint-limit safety for human-robot interaction.
card.key_idea: Analytical feedforward cancellation reduces the robot to a constant-state linear double integrator, enabling a fast convex QP with Kalman-augmented disturbance estimation.
card.evaluation: Simulated on a 7-DOF Franka FR3; achieved <0.05mm steady-state error vs 44.8mm for classical impedance under 15N force.
card.limitation: Validated only in simulation; physical hardware demonstration and energy-tank passivity certification are listed as future work.

slides.title: From 'What' to 'How' and 'Why': Sharing LLM-Generated Retrospective Summaries of Older Adults' Passive Tracking Data with Remote Family Members
slides.tldr: LLM-GENERATED NARRATIVE SUMMARIES FOR ELDERLY CARE
slides.highlight: This work explores using LLMs to transform multi-modal tracking data into context-aware narratives for remote family members, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement.

card.one_liner: LLM-generated retrospective summaries of passive tracking data help remote family members monitor older adults' well-being.
card.key_idea: A multi-layer, multi-agent LLM framework that transforms multi-modal sensing data into insight-driven, context-aware narratives, moving from objective statistics to qualitative 'how' and 'why' explanations.
card.evaluation: Interviews and a comparative survey with 11 remote family members showed significant improvements in satisfaction, trust, and perceived helpfulness over initial versions.
card.limitation: Potential for ambiguous or underspecified inferences and information loss during multi-layer data aggregation.

slides.title: Ouvia: A User-centered Framework for Measuring Usability of Speech Translation in Real-World Communication Scenarios
slides.highlight: Ouvia provides a framework for measuring the usability of speech translation in real-world one-to-one communication. This is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and listener modeling in hybrid human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: Ouvia is a user-centered framework measuring the real-world usability of speech translation across diverse demographics.
card.key_idea: A multi-phase protocol involving senders, receivers, and bilingual validators to assess usability via satisfaction, trust, and reliance, emphasizing QA-based metrics over holistic quality scores.
card.evaluation: 1,738 interactions across four ST systems (English-to-Portuguese) in healthcare and everyday scenarios; tested across three English dialects and two genders.
card.limitation: Limited to one language pair and uses clean, read speech rather than spontaneous, noisy real-world communication.
